atoms.canonical_statement: The investigators report nine additional cases of minocycline-associated non-autoimmune thyroiditis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We report an additional nine cases of minocycline associated non-autoimmune thyroiditis.

atoms.canonical_statement: The Boston Children's Hospital electronic medical record was queried for thyroid disorder and tetracycline-antibiotic codes among outpatient endocrine presentations from January 1, 2000 through July 1, 2018.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The Boston Children’s Hospital Electronic Medical Record was queried using the ICD-9 or ICD-10 code for thyroid disorder and tetracycline antibiotic.

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with thyroid cancer, congenital hypothyroidism, thyroid nodules, Trisomy 21, or type 1 diabetes mellitus were excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with thyroid cancer, congenital hypothyroidism, thyroid nodules, Trisomy 21, or type 1 diabetes mellitus were excluded.

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients taking lithium salts, amiodarone, or anti-seizure drugs, and patients with anti-TPO or anti-thyroglobulin antibodies indicating thyroid autoimmunity, were excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: patients who were taking medications known to affect thyroid function such as lithium salts, amiodarone, anti-seizure drugs or who had evidence of thyroid autoimmunity

population.label: EMR-screened outpatient endocrine patients
exclusion_criteria: evidence of thyroid autoimmunity by TPO or Tg antibodies

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients were included if TSH, total T4, or free T4 was outside the reference range at any time.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients were included if they had a thyrotropin stimulating hormone (TSH), thyroxine (T4), or free thyroxine (Free T4) level outside of the reference range at any time.

population.label: EMR-screened outpatient endocrine patients
inclusion_criteria: abnormal TSH, total T4, or free T4 at any time

atoms.canonical_statement: Non-autoimmune thyroiditis was defined as TSH below 0.3 uIU/mL with elevated free or total T4 and undetectable anti-thyroid antibodies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Non-autoimmune thyroiditis was defined as an abnormally low or suppressed thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH < 0.3 uIU/mL) and elevated free thyroxine or total thyroxine, and undetectable anti-thyroid antibodies.

outcome.definition: TSH < 0.3 uIU/mL plus elevated free T4 or total T4 and undetectable anti-thyroid antibodies
outcome.measurement_method: thyroid function testing and anti-thyroid antibody testing

atoms.canonical_statement: All nine thyroiditis cases occurred in adolescents aged 14-17 years receiving minocycline for acne; reported minocycline exposure ranged from 6 months to 4 years when duration was known.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cases of thyroiditis occurred in adolescents ages 14 – 17 years who had been taking minocycline for six months to 4 years. In all cases, minocycline was prescribed for the treatment of acne.

exposures.details: Prescribed for acne; duration 6 months to 4 years when known.

atoms.canonical_statement: Four of nine thyroiditis cases received treatment for thyrotoxicosis: beta-blockade in three cases and an anti-thyroid drug in two cases, with overlap in at least one case.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Four of the 9 received treatment for thyrotoxicosis with a beta-blocker (3 cases) and/or anti-thyroid drug (2 cases).

atoms.canonical_statement: Thyroiditis resolved after a median of 4.5 months, with a reported range of 2 to 5 months.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All thyroiditis was transient and resolved after a median of 4.5 months (range 2 – 5 months).

atoms.canonical_statement: One of nine thyroiditis cases was followed by transient hypothyroidism.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In one case, thyroiditis was followed by transient hypothyroidism.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: In one case, thyroiditis was followed by transient hypothyroidism.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1: A 17-year-old male developed symptomatic thyrotoxicosis about 11 months after starting oral minocycline 200 mg/day for acne; thyroid antibodies were negative, I-123 uptake was low, symptoms resolved within 1 month after discontinuation, and euthyroidism returned by 3 months.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 17-year-old male developed tachycardia, palpitations, myalgias, insomnia, and restlessness approximately 11 months after starting oral minocycline 200 mg daily for the treatment of acne.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors propose that minocycline-associated thyroiditis is a self-limiting destructive process caused by thyroid accumulation of minocycline or metabolites, TPO-mediated oxidation, follicular-cell cytotoxicity, and release of preformed thyroid hormone.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we propose that minocycline concentrates in the thyroid follicular cells where it and/or its metabolites are oxidized by TPO leading to cytotoxic damage and release of preformed thyroid hormone.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that anti-thyroid medication may not be warranted for this destructive thyroiditis and note that methimazole did not hasten resolution in the two treated cases.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Treatment with anti-thyroid medications which inhibit thyroid hormone formation may not be warranted, and in the two reported cases, methimazole failed to hasten resolution of thyroiditis.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommend discontinuing minocycline, using beta-blockade for symptoms when indicated, and monitoring thyroid function when minocycline-associated thyroiditis is identified.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: minocycline associated thyroiditis should be treated similar to other forms of drug induced thyroiditis, with discontinuation of minocycline, symptomatic management with beta-blockade if indicated, and laboratory monitoring of thyroid function.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that evidence is insufficient to recommend routine thyroid-function monitoring for all patients taking minocycline, but a history of minocycline exposure should be elicited in patients presenting with thyrotoxicosis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although there is not enough evidence to recommend routine monitoring of thyroid function, we do suggest that a history of minocycline exposure be elicited in any patient presenting with thyrotoxicosis while taking minocycline.

atoms.canonical_statement: Clinicians prescribing minocycline should be aware of possible thyroiditis, counsel patients about symptoms of thyrotoxicosis, and ask about minocycline use when evaluating thyroiditis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Clinicians prescribing minocycline should be aware of its potential to cause thyroiditis and should counsel patients regarding the symptoms of thyrotoxicosis.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors call for further studies to determine the cause and frequency of minocycline-induced thyroiditis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Further studies are needed to determine the cause and frequency of minocycline-induced thyroiditis.

atoms.canonical_statement: The report is limited by its retrospective design and single study site.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our report is limited by its retrospective nature and single study site.

atoms.canonical_statement: Follow-up information was limited because many patients did not return after symptom resolution.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Follow up information was limited, especially as most patients had a resolution of their symptoms and did not return for further evaluation.

atoms.canonical_statement: The observational association between minocycline use and thyroiditis cannot establish causality.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although we have noted an association between minocycline use and the development of thyroiditis, we cannot establish causality in this observational study.

extraction_limitations: The source is a retrospective single-center case series/chart review and cannot establish causality.
Follow-up was incomplete for some cases; exposure duration and/or dose were not reported for every case.
The denominator is an EMR query/review cohort rather than all patients exposed to minocycline, so incidence among minocycline users cannot be estimated from this report.
Prior cases summarized in Table 2 are secondary reports within this article and were not represented as primary-study atoms.
No external guideline, label, or current-practice verification was performed because it was not requested.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated case-report/case-series narrative object, so each individual case is represented as an adverse_event atom with one principal quantitative thyroid-hormone result while additional case details remain in the canonical statement and source excerpt.
The schema has no dedicated recommendation atom kind; source-authored practice suggestions are represented as author_conclusion atoms.
